biodiversity_overview.text: 23,542 GBIF occurrence records for 89 tracked species are attributed to Andhra Pradesh, spanning 1825-2026.
22,138 of these records (94.0%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 27, Magnoliopsida 17, Mammalia 16, Actinopterygii 13, Squamata 8, Testudines 4, Amphibia 2, Crocodylia 1, Cephalopoda 1.

threatened_species.text: 9 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
4 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Sloth Bear (VU), Asian Elephant (EN), Mugger Crocodile (VU), Tiger (EN).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Roller (2,154), White-throated Munia (1,677), Indian Pied Starling (1,659), Indian Golden Oriole (1,566), Indian Robin (1,553).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 670 in 2016 to 512 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 5.4% of Andhra Pradesh's area (19 areas intersect the state).
12.4% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (2,754 of 22,138); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Star Tortoise (0.61), Indian Scad (0.48), Small Indian Mongoose (0.47), Indian Courser (0.47), Mugger Crocodile (0.46).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Andhra Pradesh (equal-weight reference): cell near 17.625N 82.875E (overall rank 23, median rank across weightings 37); cell near 17.625N 83.625E (overall rank 29, median rank across weightings 45); cell near 18.375N 83.625E (overall rank 61, median rank across weightings 77).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 12,639 km2 (7.86% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

484.1 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (3.83% of the 2000 extent; 1.67% in 2015-2024, rank 10 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2011 (39.54 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 0.85% of land and population density is 331.4 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
28% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
GHSL R2023A built-up and population 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
